metadata.description: YouthTempo starts with everyday rhythms, helping young people understand how they are doing, express what they feel, and connect with trusted support more easily.

footer.description: Young people can check in with daily life and put feelings into words. With permission, parents and educators can understand changes and help connect them with the right support when needed.
footer.tagline: Start with what life has felt like lately.

rhythm.ariaLabel: The five everyday dimensions of the SWEET model

metadata.title: YouthTempo | Earlier support for young people

hero.label: A youth mental health support platform
hero.title: How have things been lately?
hero.description: Start with sleep, meals, movement, schoolwork and emotions. A simple check-in can make it easier to understand what is going on and talk with someone you trust when you need support.
hero.imageAlt: A young person moving forward at their own pace, supported by family, educators and a professional

demo.title: Choose what feels closest and see how a check-in can help
demo.description: You can try this example without saving anything. After you choose, you will see a short reflection and one small step you could take right away.

panel.question: How did it feel to get started this morning?

steady.label: Going fairly well
steady.summary: Your morning rhythm felt fairly steady today.
steady.step: Keep what is already helping. You do not need to add another task.

slow.label: Taking some effort
slow.summary: Getting started took some effort this morning. It is worth noticing without blaming yourself.
slow.step: Begin with the smallest next thing, such as washing up, having some water or packing your bag.

stuck.label: Hard to get started
stuck.summary: It felt hard to get going this morning. Sleep or stress may also be affecting you.
stuck.step: Reduce what you need to do to one step, or tell an adult you trust that today feels difficult.

dailyChanges.label: Why start with daily life
dailyChanges.title: Changes often show up in everyday life first
dailyChanges.description: Poor sleep, low appetite, less movement or difficulty starting schoolwork can appear before someone can say, “I feel under a lot of pressure.” Noticing these changes can help you decide whether you need rest, a conversation or more support.

audiences.label: Find the right place to begin
audiences.title: Start from where you are now
audiences.description: Young people can check in and express themselves. Parents can understand and support. Educators can notice changes and help connect students with further support when needed.

teens.title: I am a young person
teens.label: Check in and express yourself
teens.text: Notice today's rhythm and make sense of feelings that are hard to explain. When you need to, you can also write something for yourself or an adult you trust.

parents.title: I am a parent
parents.label: Understand what has changed
parents.text: Look at recent patterns in sleep, eating, movement and schoolwork, then find a gentler way to start a conversation.

teachers.title: I am an educator
teachers.label: Notice meaningful changes
teachers.text: See broad changes among the students you support, understand individual situations when needed, and help connect school, family and professional support.

support.label: From check-in to support
support.title: Take it one step at a time, in the order life happens
support.description: Start with what daily life has been like, then make sense of what you are feeling. If it becomes too much to manage alone, ask someone you trust to think through the next step with you.

daily.title: Start with recent daily life
daily.label: Sleep, meals, movement and schoolwork
daily.text: You do not need to explain everything at once. Begin with the clearest change from the past few days.

feelings.title: Put the feeling into words
feelings.label: Emotions and pressure
feelings.text: Choose a few words that feel close, or write down the concern that keeps coming back.

people.title: Ask someone to help when needed
people.label: Family, educators or professional support
people.text: If it feels too hard to carry alone, tell someone you trust what has been happening and decide together who to turn to next.

principles.label: Our approach
principles.title: A check-in helps describe what is happening. It does not define anyone.

items.one: 1. One check-in will never be used to draw a conclusion about you
items.two: 2. Reflections only organise what you choose to share
items.three: 3. When needed, we will encourage you to contact someone you trust

hero.label: For young people
hero.title: A place to start
hero.description: Whether you want to understand how you have been doing, untangle one difficult thought, or write down something that is hard to say face to face, you can begin here.
hero.imageAlt: A student holding a notebook and preparing to check in at her own pace

start.title: Where would you like to start today?
start.description: Choose just one thing at a time.

rhythm.title: I want to see how I am doing today
rhythm.text: Check in with sleep, waking, eating, movement and task engagement to capture today's real-life rhythm.
rhythm.alt: A daily rhythm made up of sleep, waking, eating, movement and task engagement

mood.title: I cannot quite explain how I feel
mood.text: You do not need to explain everything yet. Choose a few emotions that feel close, then add what happened when you are ready.
mood.alt: A mood mosaic made from different colours

talk.title: I want somewhere to talk
talk.text: Start with the one thing that feels most stuck and work through it one question at a time.
talk.alt: A tangled feeling gradually becoming clearer

messages.title: I want to tell a parent or educator something
messages.text: If it is hard to say face to face, write it down and choose whether to share it with a parent, an educator, or keep it for yourself.

worry.title: My thoughts keep going at bedtime
worry.text: Write down what is worrying you, then separate what you can act on from what can wait.
worry.alt: Setting worries down gently under moonlight

referral.title: I want to know what to do next
referral.text: If pressure has continued for days or is clearly affecting daily life or learning, explore a support path that fits.
referral.action: Find the next source of support
referral.alt: A gentle path leading towards appropriate support

youngAdults.title: 18 or older and want to use YouthTempo independently?
youngAdults.description: Young adults aged 18–25 can complete their own informed confirmation without involving a school or guardian.

support.title: Has it felt hard to keep going lately?
support.description: Start by talking with an adult or educator you trust. You can also explore which kind of support may fit.
support.action: Find the next source of support

feedback.title: Is there anything you would change?
feedback.description: Take two minutes to tell us what felt easy and where you got stuck.

hero.label: For parents
hero.title: Support starts with noticing
hero.description: Begin with how your child has been sleeping, eating and moving, then find a calm, non-judgmental way to start a conversation.
hero.imageAlt: A parent listening calmly and preparing to support their child

intro.visibleText: You can only view records for a child whose relationship to you has been confirmed by the school. You cannot see information about other students. One check-in never tells the whole story; it is a way to understand what has been happening and begin a conversation.
intro.concreteTitle: Start with a specific change before asking why
intro.concreteText: For many young people, answering “What is wrong with you?” is difficult. It can be easier to begin with something concrete, such as poor sleep, difficulty getting up, or struggling to start schoolwork.

starts.title: Where can parents begin?
starts.description: Choose the most specific starting point that is least likely to create conflict.

daily.title: Notice recent daily life
daily.text: Start with sleep, waking, meals, movement and schoolwork, and notice whether any changes have continued.
daily.alt: A father and daughter looking through the five SWEET daily rhythms together

listen.title: Lower defensiveness first
listen.text: Focus on understanding your child's experience instead of immediately judging, asking for reasons or demanding change.
listen.alt: A parent setting judgment aside and listening quietly

conversation.title: Find an easier opening line
conversation.text: Say what you have noticed and why you care, then choose a time when neither of you will be interrupted.
conversation.alt: A parent and child moving through a safe conversation step by step

support.title: Connect with support when needed
support.text: When changes continue to affect daily life or learning, family, school and professional support can work together.
support.alt: A parent helping their child connect with school and professional support

messages.title: Read messages your child has shared
messages.description: Messages a child chooses to share with a parent are collected on a separate page.

feedback.title: How did YouthTempo feel to use?
feedback.description: Take two minutes to tell us what helped and what still needs improvement.

sweet.title: What parents can notice with SWEET
sweet.description: SWEET organises daily life into five observable areas. A change does not necessarily mean something is seriously wrong, but if it continues, it is worth checking in with your child.

sleep.title: Sleep
sleep.question: Has sleep been fairly steady?
sleep.text: Notice whether bedtime, waking during the night or morning tiredness feels clearly different from before.

wake.title: Waking up
wake.question: Is it much harder to get started in the morning?
wake.text: Notice whether getting up, washing, leaving home or beginning the day has become more difficult.

eat.title: Eating
eat.question: Have meals been regular?
eat.text: Notice changes in energy, appetite, skipped meals or relying on snacks to get through the day.

exercise.title: Movement
exercise.question: Has physical activity noticeably decreased?
exercise.text: Notice whether your child is going out, moving or joining familiar activities less often.

task.title: Task engagement
task.question: Is it hard to begin school or everyday tasks?
task.text: Look beyond the outcome and notice whether starting and staying with a task have become harder.

aidet.title: Using AIDET to start a conversation
aidet.description: AIDET breaks a conversation into five steps. You do not need to use the terminology—simply follow the order to make your care clear.

acknowledge.label: Acknowledge your child's experience
acknowledge.example: I know you may be genuinely tired lately. I don't think you're doing this on purpose.

introduce.label: Explain why you are here
introduce.example: I'm not here to criticise you. I just want to understand how things have been lately.

duration.label: Keep the conversation manageable
duration.example: Let's talk for ten minutes. We don't need to solve everything right now.

explanation.label: Explain why daily rhythms matter
explanation.example: Sleep, waking, eating and movement can affect emotions and attention. I'd like to see if there is one place where we can make things a little easier.

thankYou.label: Thank them for sharing
thankYou.example: Thank you for telling me. I know this may not be easy to talk about.

conversation.title: Words you can use
conversation.description: You do not need to follow these lines exactly. Choose one that sounds natural in your own voice and let the conversation begin.

phrases.one: Have you been feeling tired lately? I'd like to listen first.
phrases.two: Let's talk for ten minutes. We don't need to solve it right now.
phrases.three: It's okay if you don't know how to explain it yet.
phrases.four: I won't judge. Which part has felt most tiring lately?

furtherSupport.title: When to seek further support
furtherSupport.label: Connect with more support
furtherSupport.text: If pressure continues or clearly affects sleep, learning, relationships or daily life, families can consider school-based mental health support or a qualified counsellor, and connect with medical or emergency services when necessary. The goal is not to blame anyone, but to help the young person receive appropriate support.

oneThing.title: One thing parents can do first
oneThing.text: Begin with one specific change, such as poor sleep, difficulty getting up, or struggling to start schoolwork. Explain that you only want to understand what has been happening, then listen to what your child says.

resources.title: Family and school support guide
resources.text: Practical approaches for parents and educators to understand young people's rhythms, feelings and support needs earlier.

hero.label: For educators
hero.title: Notice change, then start a conversation
hero.description: Begin with whether the students you support have shown ongoing changes. When needed, understand the specific situation and decide with the student whether to involve family or further support.
hero.imageAlt: An educator holding a notebook and preparing to listen to a student

week.title: Start with the past week
week.description: See which students have checked in recently and where daily patterns may have continued to change.
week.alt: An educator reviewing an overview of changes among the students she supports

details.title: Understand the specific situation
details.description: When needed, review a student's recent reflections and own records, then begin with the concrete change you have noticed.
details.alt: An educator and student reviewing the five SWEET daily rhythms together

listen.title: Hear from the student
listen.description: Read messages students found difficult to say face to face and chose to share with an educator.
listen.alt: Reviewing a private message shared by a student

conversation.title: Use a check-in to begin a conversation
conversation.text: When sleep, eating, movement or task engagement continues to change, begin with a simple question: “Has something been making things feel more tiring lately?” Listen first, then decide together whether more support is needed.

feedback.title: What could work more smoothly?
feedback.description: Take two minutes to share what using YouthTempo was like and help us improve the pilot.

hero.label: For ages 18–25
hero.title: You do not have to wait until everything feels settled to care for your rhythm.
hero.description: Leaving school, starting university or beginning work can bring more freedom—and make daily life easier to lose track of. You can use YouthTempo independently, without involving a school or guardian.
hero.imageAlt: A path of growth moving forward at an individual pace

tools.title: Start with what you need right now
tools.description: Choose one thing at a time. This does not need to become another task list.

rhythm.title: Check in with your recent rhythm
rhythm.text: Start with sleep, waking, eating, movement and the tasks in front of you. You do not need to understand every problem first.
rhythm.alt: A check-in path made up of five everyday rhythms

mood.title: Put a complicated feeling into words
mood.text: When emotions feel mixed, choose what feels closest and add what just happened when you are ready.
mood.alt: A mood mosaic made from different colours

worry.title: Set worries down before sleep
worry.text: Separate what you can act on from what cannot be handled yet. You do not need to solve everything tonight.

support.title: Know where to turn for human support
support.text: When things continue to affect study, work or daily life, find a source of support that fits the level of urgency.
support.action: Find the next source of support
support.alt: A path connecting someone with appropriate support step by step

confirmation.label: Independent confirmation
confirmation.title: If you are 18 or older, you can confirm for yourself
confirmation.text: After signing in, select “18 or older,” read the data information and confirm. You do not need guardian consent or school membership.

records.label: Your records
records.title: Only you can see them by default
records.text: If you are not part of a school, no school or educator can view your records. You can export your data, delete individual entries or close your account.

boundary.label: What YouthTempo is not
boundary.title: It is not a diagnostic or emergency service
boundary.text: If you are in immediate danger of harming yourself or someone else, contact local emergency services, the police, or someone nearby who can be with you now.

teens.title: Still part of the school pilot for ages 14–18?
teens.description: The youth area includes support relationships with parents, educators and schools.
